title: 1 shuffle: a guesser names 31 of 52 cards. 7 shuffles: 5. Chance: 4.5.
description:
A 52-card deck starts in factory order and is riffle shuffled with the Gilbert-Shannon-Reeds model (cut at Binomial(52, 1/2), every interleaving equally likely). Ten thousand decks are shuffled ten times each from seed 0 (numpy RandomState), keeping the deck after every shuffle, plus ten thousand uniformly random decks. A guesser who knows the factory order and remembers every card it has seen names one card before each card is turned: the first card of the longest run of unseen consecutive ranks, ties to the run that continues the card just seen. Any such guesser scores H_52 = 4.54 on a random deck, pure chance.

Measured at seed 0, average right guesses of 52 over 10,000 decks:
- 1 shuffle: 31.18; 2: 19.67; 3: 12.92; 4: 8.79; 5: 6.59; 6: 5.49; 7: 5.01; 8: 4.78; 9: 4.66; 10: 4.61; random deck: 4.55 (chance 4.54)
- edge over chance: 26.6, 15.1, 8.4, 4.3, 2.1, 1.0, 0.5, then 0.25, 0.12, 0.08: about half of it survives each riffle
- decks where the guesser scores above 10: 100%, 100%, 84.8%, 20.6%, 3.0%, 0.9%, 0.3% for 1 to 7 shuffles; 0.1% of random decks
- exact total variation distance from a random deck (Bayer-Diaconis formula, exact Eulerian numbers): 1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 0.924, 0.614, 0.334, 0.167, 0.085, 0.043 for 1 to 10 shuffles
- mean rising sequences: 2.0, 4.0, 8.0, 14.1, 19.6, 22.9, 24.7 for 1 to 7 shuffles; random 26.5

The rows on screen show the one deck whose tallies sit closest to the row averages (31, 19, 13, 9, 7, 6, 5 right) and one random deck (5 right); the bar chart shows the running averages over all 10,000 decks per row.

Why: after k riffles the deck is an interleaving of at most 2^k rising runs of the factory order. While the runs are long the guesser reads them; once there are more runs than cards can fill, the deck is random to any guesser.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
